This was a relief week. Every major fund and every sector finished higher, and the VIX dropped from 25.6 to 19.3. Still, one good week doesn't erase a rough month: QQQ is down 8.6% and tech is down 13.2% since mid-October.

Zoom out to the year and the story is value and defensive stocks, not growth. Health care, staples and energy have carried the market while the growth fund is up less than 4%. The question now is whether tech's bounce sticks or fades.

Inflation is the thing to watch. CPI is running at 4.1% and rising, which is now above the 3.88% Fed funds rate, and the 2-year yield has climbed 139 bps this year. The next CPI report and how the Fed responds will set the tone, with 30-year mortgages already at 7.11%.
Individual investors aren't buying the rally yet. Bearish sentiment hit 51.4%, and bears have outnumbered bulls for four weeks straight. If that climbs past 60% it reaches the method's Strong level.
